thread:
ren: Rolling eclipse-q (int8) canary - canary-207. We're seeing funcall/toolcall parse failures around 1.7% in the last 90m. Samples hint at an EOS-like control token showing up mid-JSON which causes streaming parsers to cut early.

tara: can you paste a raw failing capture and canary id?

ren: canary-207. mirror capture:```
{"call":"fetch_items","args":{"ids":[1,2,3],"meta":"ok"}
```
chunk ended right after a backslash-escaped newline in a string. parser: "Unexpected end of input". Token tail (mirror token-log): `..., 301, 12, 0, 88` where `0` looks like an injected control/EOS.

evan: interesting. instead of full json-wrap or gateway buffering, what if we try an "eos-squeeze" heuristic in the streaming combiner: when token id 0 appears at chunk boundary and the following bytes would complete a valid close (e.g., see immediate `]}` ahead), we drop the control token before handing to parser. Lower cost than buffering full suffix.

yuki: risky but worth a canary test. We need to ensure this only applies to funcall routes and we log every dropped-control event for audits. Also add a "safety backoff": if more than X drops per minute, disable and fallback to full buffer.

stream-bot: alert: funcall_parse_error rate for eclipse-q/int8 = 1.7% -> 2.4% over 30m. threshold 0.5% breached.

tara: quick repro: implemented a prototype eos-squeeze on canary route. It inspects token provenance and when token 0 occurs at end-of-chunk, peeks at next chunk bytes for immediate closers. If closing braces found within next 64 bytes, drop the control token and stitch.

ren: results from 45m A/B: parse errors dropped 1.7% -> 0.28%. median latency +9ms. metrics: `errors:[1.7,0.28], p50_ms:[130,139]`. No semantic delta on our 1k paired check set vs fp16.

evan: good. logs show ~220 dropped-controls in 45m on the canary (all for funcall endpoints), all logged with token tails and mirror traces. No safety backoff triggered.

yuki: plan proposals:
1) keep eos-squeeze enabled only for canary-tool routes for 12h and collect repair logs
2) run a 5k paired eval (int8 vs fp16) for semantic drift focusing on toolcall outputs; nina to run this (assign later)
3) add automated auditing: every dropped-control gets a ticketed artifact and is included in weekly parse-failure digests
4) prototype a token-layer fix in quantizer to avoid inserting control token 0 mid-string (longer-term)

ren: owners: @tara keep canary toggle and dashboard, @evan add logging hook + ticket artifacts, @yuki own gating thresholds & fallback to fp16 if drop_rate spike.

tara: note: if eos-squeeze starts masking a real truncation where the trailing chunk is lost entirely (not just a control token), we should fail open and revert to suffix-buffer. We'll add a cheap checksum: if we drop a control token but the stitched JSON still fails schema-lint, treat as a non-silent repair and increment a counter.

evan: prefix note: this is intentionally conservative - we only drop control token when parser would have otherwise failed due to a single extraneous token and the next bytes show an immediate closer. Not applied for streaming multi-shard ensembles.

yuki: gating update: set canary max parse_error = 0.7% for 30m. production block if parse_error > 1.0% for 10m.

stream-bot: note: automated rollback policy: production routes roll back if funcall_parse_error_rate > 1.0% sustained for 15m.

ren: ok proceeding with 12h canary run. I'll open CAN-7732 and attach the 220 drop logs + mirror traces. Follow-up in 3h with 1h snapshot. :thumbsup:
